title: Standard Days Method (CycleBeads)
path: Fertility Awareness and Natural Family Planning

headings.title: Introduction to the Standard Days Method
headings.content: The **Standard Days Method** (SDM) is a modern natural family planning approach based on the biological reality of the human menstrual cycle. It identifies a fixed window of the cycle when a woman is fertile, allowing couples to either avoid or achieve pregnancy without hormones or devices inside the body. Developed by the Institute for Reproductive Health at Georgetown University, this method relies on the physiological observation that ovulation typically occurs within a specific timeframe, and sperm can survive in the female reproductive tract for up to five days. SDM targets women with regular cycles, making cycle length predictability the foundational requirement for safe use.

headings.title: Client Selection Criteria
headings.content:
Not every woman is a suitable candidate for the Standard Days Method. Proper screening during antenatal or family planning clinics prevents unintended pregnancies. A client must meet specific baseline characteristics before adoption:

- **Cycle Length**: Her menstrual cycles must consistently be between 26 and 32 days long.
- **Cycle Regularity**: She must not have more than one cycle per year that falls outside the 26 to 32-day range.
- **Desire for Pregnancy**: She and her partner must be willing to abstain from unprotected intercourse or use barrier methods during the fertile days.
- **Postpartum Status**: If recently postpartum, she must wait until her regular cycles return before starting.

headings.title: Mechanism of Cycle Tracking
headings.content: The biological logic of the Standard Days Method isolates days **8 through 19** of the menstrual cycle as the fixed fertile window. Day one is defined as the very first day of full menstrual bleeding. Even though ovulation timing can vary slightly from month to month, population studies show that restricting unprotected intercourse during this 12-day block covers the statistical probability of ovulation and sperm survival. If a woman has a single cycle shorter than 26 days or longer than 32 days, the mathematical safety margin collapses, and she steps outside the efficacy parameters of the method.

headings.title: Use of CycleBeads
headings.content:
**CycleBeads** are a physical, color-coded tool designed to help a woman track her cycle days easily without complicated record-keeping or literacy barriers. The tool consists of a ring with small beads representing each day of the cycle:

- **Red Bead**: Represents Day 1 of the menstrual cycle (the start of her period).
- **Brown Beads**: Represent safe days when pregnancy is unlikely.
- **White Beads**: Represent fertile days (days 8 through 19) when unprotected sex can lead to pregnancy.
- **Dark Bead with a Ring**: A movable rubber ring is placed on the red bead on day one and moved forward one bead each day, regardless of whether she has bleeding or intercourse.

headings.title: Counseling and Efficacy in Nigerian Clinical Practice
headings.content: Implementing the Standard Days Method in Nigerian health facilities requires clear, culturally sensitive communication. Midwives must ensure that both partners understand the shared responsibility of abstinence or barrier use during the white bead days. With correct and consistent use, the method has a typical failure rate of about 5%, making it comparable to other barrier methods. However, in busy clinical environments, midwives must screen for irregular cycles caused by nutritional stress, fibroids, or perimenopause. If a woman's cycle falls outside the 26-32 day limit twice within a year, counseling must guide her to transition to an alternative contraceptive method.
